thread:
sara: :rotating_light: acme-corp reporting 429s against our dedicated pool eu-west-1-gold since ~09:12 UTC. They say requests suddenly started routing to a shared cold pool and throttling. Can someone triage?

tim: saw the alert too. their tenant id = tenant-acme-42. I see elevated 429s in proxy logs and a drop in capacity for gold. Not matching autoscale events.

raj: pinging @eng-oncall-bot and @maureen for routing/control-plane. quick dump from proxy: 
```
[09:12:03] proxy: req id=.. tenant=tenant-acme-42 tier=gold route=controlplane-eval->shared-cold pool=shared-cold token_bucket=0/100 limit=100
[09:12:04] proxy: 429 serve throttle cause=rate_limit pool=shared-cold
```

maureen: hmm that log shows controlplane matched fallback pool 'shared-cold' even though tenant has dedicated mapping to eu-west-1-gold. can you paste the routing decision record (redwood-controlplane trace) for one of those requests?

tim: pasted snippet from controlplane trace for req-id .. :
```
decision: selectors matched [tenant_attr, header_tier]
eval_order: [header_tier, priority_map, tenant_override]
applied: priority_map -> pool: shared-cold
note: tenant_override rule present but evaluated after priority_map
```

sara: so tenant_override existed but wasn't applied before priority_map? that sounds like an eval-order bug. customer says they didn't change config.

maureen: agreed. expected eval order is tenant_override first, then tenant-tier mapping, then priority_map. if priority_map wins prematurely it can route to shared pools.

lee: repro steps I used locally: curl to api with header 'X-Redwood-Tier: gold' and tenant header 'X-Tenant-ID: tenant-acme-42' -> got routed to shared-cold when priority_map contains a generic entry for 'eu-west-1' with higher precedence. command: 
```
curl -v -H 'X-Tenant-ID: tenant-acme-42' -H 'X-Redwood-Tier: gold' https://api.eu-west-1.redwood.example/generate
```
response: 429, header X-Redwood-Pool: shared-cold

tim: temporary mitigation for ACME: I patched controlplane config to add a tenant-scoped override with explicit priority + locked precedence ahead of global priority_map. applied at 09:25 UTC. customer reports reduced 429s after the patch. :thumbsup:

raj: good quick patch. still want runtime/eng-runtime to look for a regression in the policy-eval order. health-check: autoscale did not trigger because pool assignment moved traffic to shared-cold which has strict token bucket -> observed it choke. we should also check the rollout that changed eval ordering.

maureen: opening an incident and assigning to eng-runtime. initial hypothesis: recent config service change made priority_map precedence default higher than tenant_override if tenant_override is unset or has empty match. I'll attach full traces.

eng-oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-045 created, severity=P2, assigned=eng-runtime, link=https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-045

sara: ACME is on a dedicated contract, raised billing/legal escalation. keeping them updated. Thanks for fast patch.

lee: notes for repro in case eng-runtime needs them:
1) reproduce with tenant that has tenant_override present but empty metadata value -> controlplane evaulates priority_map earlier.
2) run with config version v2026-03-17-0910 vs v2026-03-16-2100 to see difference in eval ordering.

maureen: action items:
- eng-runtime: confirm eval-order regression and revert or add explicit ordering enforcement (P0).
- infra: check autoscaler metrics for eu-west-1-gold around 09:00-09:30 UTC; why didn't it trigger on rising queue depth (P1).
- support: keep ACME informed; we've applied tenant-scoped override and monitoring.

tim: adding logs/trace links in the incident.

sara: customer replied: "latency improving, 429s dropping, thanks for quick fix." will update thread when fully resolved.
